title: What To Do With An Embedded Ball
question: If your ball is embedded on the putting green after a shot, what is the correct thing to do?

choices.text: Leave it and play it as it lies
Mark its position, lift the ball, repair the pitch-mark, and replace the ball
Pick it up and drop it two club lengths away
Ask another player to move it for you

explanation: You should mark where the ball is, lift it, repair the pitch-mark, and then replace the ball without any penalty.

juniorVersion.title: What Should You Do If Your Ball Stuck Into The Green?
juniorVersion.question: If your ball lands on the putting green and gets stuck in its own hole, what should you do?

choices.text: Leave it where it is and hit it from there.
Put a marker where your ball is, pick it up, fix the little hole, and put your ball back.
Pick up the ball and drop it two club lengths away.
Ask someone else to move it for you.

juniorVersion.explanation: You should put a marker next to your ball, pick it up, fix the hole it made, and then put your ball back in the same spot.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The short, smooth grass around the hole where you finish the hole.
When your ball is stuck down in the ground after it lands.
A small hole made when the ball lands hard on the green.
A small flat object you use to show where your ball was.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Let children practise marking their golf ball, fixing a pitch-mark, and replacing the ball on the green in a safe space.
likelyMisconceptions: Some children may think they have to play the ball while it is still stuck in the ground.
Some may think they need to drop the ball somewhere else.
Some may think someone else should pick up their ball.
